title: sidecar-siphon-sampled-routing-and-tenant-metering
creator: Priya Nair
description: Introduce a sidecar-based 'siphon' pipeline to copy a bounded fraction of production requests to non-impacting observer paths. Goals: safely exercise canary and A/B candidates without affecting latency/availability of the primary path; provide per-tenant cost metering and automatic throttles; ensure fast, reversible rollback when regressions are detected. This ticket implements sampling, tenant-level budget fences, request sanitization for PII, metrics hooks for fidelity checks, and a lightweight control plane to configure siphon policies per route and environment.
design_notes: Architecture: sidecar (envoy filter) duplicates request metadata and a minimal payload to a separate gRPC siphon service. The siphon service performs lightweight authorization, applies per-tenant sampling decisions, and forwards a copy to a 'replay' endpoint in the canary cluster or a shadow ingest queue.

Sampling strategy: hybrid deterministic+probing. Default deterministic sampling uses hashed tenant_id + route to provide reproducible sampling percentages. A short-lived probing mode (2% traffic for 1 hour) is available for new models to surface emergent issues with low cost.

Budgeting & metering: each tenant has a monthly quota for siphon traffic (in token-equivalents). The siphon service consults a fast in-memory quota store (with consistent hashing) and falls back to a best-effort allowlist when quota store is unreachable. Over-quota -> sample down to 0% and emit alert.

Isolation: siphon copies must never touch production state. All copied requests are annotated and routed to read-only canary replicas or isolated test pools. Writes are scrubbed and blocked at the sidecar.

Cost controls: backpressure tokens and rate-limit leases prevent sudden bursts of siphon traffic from overwhelming canary pools. A global cost governor enforces a cap (initially 5% of cluster capacity) with tenant-level soft caps.

Observability: fidelity metric compares canary output distribution to prod (token-level delta, latency distribution, hallucination signals). Dashboards and alerting hooks created under grafana: /d/traffic-siphon/siphon-fidelity.

Rollback semantics: automatic rollback triggers when fidelity regression score exceeds threshold for 5m window OR if canary latency tail breaches configured SLO. Control plane supports immediate pause and gradual drain of siphon traffic.

Security: PII redaction performed via prompt sanitizer library. All siphon payloads encrypted at rest; logs annotated to avoid storing raw user content. We require an internal security review before enabling tenant-level siphon policies.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar successfully copies requests for a test route in staging with deterministic sampling enabled and copied requests visible in the canary ingestion queue.
Per-tenant quota enforcement works: when tenant quota is exhausted, sampling drops to 0% and a billing event is emitted.
No production latency regression observed at 99th percentile under synthetic load up to 1.5x baseline.
Fidelity dashboard shows token-distribution deltas for canary vs production and fires synthetic regression alerts when introduced test anomalies occur.
Automatic pause API can pause siphon traffic within 30s and gracefully drain in-flight copies.
Security review completed and PII redaction demoed in staging with audit logs enabled.
implementation_steps: 1) Envoy sidecar filter prototype to duplicate request context and payload summary -> siphon service (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar-siphon#12).
2) Siphon service: sampling engine + quota consult + routing to shadow ingestion topic. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/siphon-service#47).
3) Canary ingest adapter to accept copies on read-only canary pools and attach metadata for traceability. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/canary-adapter#9).
4) Add Grafana dashboards and fidelity alert rules (grafana: /d/traffic-siphon/siphon-fidelity).
5) Integration tests for end-to-end sampling, quota exhaustion, and pause/rollback behavior in staging environment.
6) Gradual rollout plan: internal-only -> opt-in customers -> default off for public tenants.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: sidecar duplication could increase p99 latency if synchronous. Mitigation: duplication is async and non-blocking; sidecar only sends a small payload summary by default.

Risk: misconfigured siphon policy could accidentally route writes to canary. Mitigation: strict request sanitizer and policy tests; canary adapter enforces read-only behavior and rejects known write patterns.
Risk: cost overrun from high-cardinality tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant soft caps + global governor + billing alerting when projected monthly token delta > threshold.
Risk: quota store outage causing incorrect sampling. Mitigation: fall back to conservative default (0% for tiers without explicit allowlist) and emit high-severity alert.
notes: Design review held 2025-02-20: feedback from SRE to prioritize non-blocking paths and circuit-breaker semantics for quota store.
PM asked to add a 'preview' flag for customers to opt into siphon for their tenant; implementation tracked as ENG-21400.
Blocked on HSM integration for long-term log encryption; temporary KMS-backed storage acceptable for staging.
